name: Fat Mono
explanation: A monophonic analog synthesizer modelled control-for-control on the Moog Minimoog Model D (User's Manual Version 2, read cover to cover). Three oscillators, each with six waveforms (triangle, triangle-sawtooth hybrid — reverse sawtooth on oscillator 3 — sawtooth, square, wide pulse, narrow pulse) and six ranges (LO, 32', 16', 8', 4', 2'); oscillators 2 and 3 fine-tune +/-7 semitones; OSC. 3 CONTROL switch releases oscillator 3 from the keyboard for drones and free-running modulation. Five-source mixer (Osc 1/2/3, white/pink noise, external input) with per-source on/off rocker switches and the famous no-cable feedback overload drive (scaled by Main Output Volume, per the manual). Modulation bus: OSC. 3/FILTER EG and NOISE/LFO source switches, MODULATION MIX knob, mod wheel, OSCILLATOR MODULATION and FILTER MODULATION switches; when WHITE noise is selected the mod source is pink noise, when PINK is selected it is red noise (manual p.21). Dedicated LFO (0.05-200 Hz) with the push/pull triangle/square shape switch. 24 dB/oct ladder low-pass with Cutoff (-4..+4), self-oscillating Emphasis, Amount of Contour (0-4 octaves), and KEYBOARD CONTROL 1 (1/3) and 2 (2/3) tracking switches. Filter and Loudness contours (Attack/Decay/Sustain) with the left-hand DECAY switch that re-uses decay time as release (off = abrupt release). Glide knob + switch (1 ms - 10 s per octave), spring-loaded pitch wheel (+/-7 semitones = a fifth, manual p.24), low/high/last note priority and multi-trigger vs legato single-trigger (Global Settings p.47), A-440 reference tuner, Main Output switch, master TUNE, and the reissue's velocity-to-loudness and after-pressure-to-filter patch routes. Switch groups are bit-packed; the panel shows every individual rocker.
